html:
Bagan, on the Irrawaddy plain, was the capital of the first Burmese empire, and its kings and people built over 10,000 Buddhist temples and stupas there between the 11th and 13th centuries. More than 2,000 still stand.

After Anawrahta united the land and adopted Theravada Buddhism, building temples became the way to make merit. The Ananda Temple of 1105 and the Shwezigon are among the finest.

The empire fell after the Mongol invasions of the late 13th century, but Bagan remained a place of pilgrimage. An earthquake in 1975 damaged many temples. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019. See Pagan kingdom.
